content.title: How store policies interact with platform policy
content.body:
# How store policies interact with platform policy

Stores on Cartwheel may set their own return windows and fees. An override is valid only if it is stated on the store's own policy page. When a store policy and the platform default disagree, the store policy wins, whether it is stricter or looser than the platform default of 30 days.

steps.text:
Store overrides are store-specific return policy settings that can replace Cartwheel’s platform default return policy.

Here’s how they work:

- Cartwheel’s default return window is **30 days**.
- A store can set its own **return window** and **fees**.
- The store’s override only counts if it is **clearly stated on the store’s own policy page**.
- If the store policy and Cartwheel’s default policy disagree, the **store policy wins**.
- That applies whether the store policy is **stricter** than Cartwheel’s default, like 14 days, or **looser**, like 60 days.

Example:
- Cartwheel default: returns allowed within 30 days.
- Your store policy page says: returns allowed within 14 days.
- Result: your store’s 14-day window applies.

Another example:
- Cartwheel default: returns allowed within 30 days.
- Your store policy page says: returns allowed within 45 days.
- Result: your store’s 45-day window applies.

The key requirement is that the override must be stated on your store’s policy page. If it is not stated there, the platform default applies. Policy: **cw-store-overrides**.

content.title: When a case goes to a human
content.body:
# When a case goes to a human

Some cases always go to a human support agent: refunds above 100 dollars, account changes, disputes, and anything the assistant cannot resolve from policy and the order record. A human responds to an escalation within 24 hours.

steps.text:
If a shopper needs help with something we can’t resolve, the process is to **escalate the case to a human support agent**.

Use escalation when the issue is outside our authority or can’t be resolved from policy/order records, including:

- **Refunds above $100**
- **Account changes**
- **Disputes**
- **Anything we can’t resolve using policy and the order record**

Once escalated, **a human support agent responds within 24 hours**. Policy: **cw-escalations**.

A good handoff should include:

1. **Short summary of the issue**  
   Example: “Shopper is requesting help with a disputed charge.”

2. **Relevant context**  
   Include order ID if available, what the shopper asked for, what you checked, and why it needs a human.

3. **Set expectation with the shopper**  
   Example: “I’m going to send this to a human support agent. They’ll follow up within 24 hours.”

Don’t promise a refund or outcome before the review is complete, especially for anything above the automatic approval threshold.

content.title: Roles and permissions on Cartwheel
content.body:
# Roles and permissions on Cartwheel

Cartwheel has three roles. Shoppers can see and manage their own orders. Merchants can see and manage orders of their own store, and cannot see other stores' orders or shoppers' other purchases. Support staff can look up any order. The platform enforces these permissions in its systems; support assistants cannot grant exceptions.

steps.text:
Here’s the official breakdown from Cartwheel’s roles policy (**cw-roles**):

## Shopper visibility and permissions
Shoppers can:

- See their **own orders**
- Manage their **own orders**, where supported by order status and policy

Shoppers cannot:

- See other shoppers’ orders
- See merchant-wide order data
- See orders from stores they did not personally buy from

Source: **cw-roles**

## Merchant visibility and permissions
Merchants can:

- See and manage orders for **their own store**

Merchants cannot:

- See orders from **other stores**
- See a shopper’s purchases at **other merchants/stores**
- Access platform-wide customer or order data outside their own store context

So if a shopper bought from Store A and Store B, the Store A merchant can only see the Store A order, not the Store B purchase history. Source: **cw-roles**

## Support staff visibility and permissions
Support staff can:

- Look up **any order** on the platform for support purposes

Support access is broader than shopper or merchant access, but it is still governed by Cartwheel’s platform permissions and support rules. Source: **cw-roles**

## Exceptions
There are no manual exceptions that support assistants can grant. The platform enforces these permissions in its systems, and support assistants cannot override them. Source: **cw-roles**

In short:

| Role | Can see own orders | Can see own store’s orders | Can see all platform orders | Can see other stores’ orders |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Shopper | Yes | No | No | No |
| Merchant | No, unless it is their purchase/account context | Yes | No | No |
| Support | Yes, through support lookup | Yes, through support lookup | Yes | Yes |

Official policy cited: **cw-roles**.

# When a case goes to a human

Some cases always go to a human support agent: refunds above 100 dollars, account changes, disputes, and anything the assistant cannot resolve from policy and the order record. A human responds to an escalation within 24 hours.

steps.text:
We’re required to hand off these cases to a human support agent instead of resolving them ourselves:

1. **Refunds above $100** — these always go to a human for review rather than being completed automatically. **(cw-escalations)**
2. **Account changes** — any account-change request must be handled by a human. **(cw-escalations)**
3. **Disputes** — disputes are always handled by a human support agent. **(cw-escalations)**
4. **Anything we can’t resolve from the policy and the order record** — if the available policy guidance and order details aren’t enough to confidently resolve the case, we escalate it. **(cw-escalations)**

A human responds to an escalation within **24 hours**. **(cw-escalations)**

content.title: Roles and permissions on Cartwheel
content.body:
# Roles and permissions on Cartwheel

Cartwheel has three roles. Shoppers can see and manage their own orders. Merchants can see and manage orders of their own store, and cannot see other stores' orders or shoppers' other purchases. Support staff can look up any order. The platform enforces these permissions in its systems; support assistants cannot grant exceptions.

steps.text:
Here’s the basic visibility split on Cartwheel:

- **Shoppers** can see and manage **their own orders only**.
- **Merchants** — like your account — can see and manage **orders for your own store only**. You **can’t see other stores’ orders**, and you **can’t see a shopper’s purchases from other stores**.
- **Support staff** can look up **any order** when needed to help with support cases.
- These permissions are enforced by Cartwheel’s systems, and support assistants can’t grant exceptions.  

Policy: **cw-roles**
